title: Brother Joe's army service and musical training
summary: Joe served with the Tenth Cavalry, learned music in the army, and taught Durham on visits to his camp from about age eight.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So you were about -- well, it's about time for us to start talking about -- I asked you how you got your training and you were telling me about your oldest brother Joe and you dumbfounded me by telling me that Joe was -- had joined up with Teddy Roosevelt's Rough Riders.
Yeah, he was there.
And he was with them -- you said he was with them about four years.
Somewhere around in there. Yeah, he was young when he got (inaudible) Army and he stayed in until that last war. He was in that last war.
'That last war.' That must be the Mexican-American War, I suppose. What? The last battle or something?
(Inaudible) but I can't think of the name of that guy. They had Poncho Villa and there was another
one or was he the last guy?
Well, I --
(Inaudible). Poncho Villa.
Yeah, I think that's --
Yeah, I used to know the name well.
It wasn't Zapata, was it?
No, I think it was Poncho Villa.
Yeah, yeah.
And that's when they was fighting across the border.
Yeah. Well, that's good. That's very interesting. Oh, well, listen. So then you said that he took while he was in the Army. He got all kind of good musical training.
Sure.
And he learned to -- everything -- read and --
And then when he came out of the Army, then he really -- he kept books and he stayed deep into the music and then I was deep into getting experience from what I got off of him.
Well, you said that when you were about eight years old, you visited him and that he would give you your instruction.
(Inaudible).
: What did we say? Camp Travis?
Yeah, I forgot -- that's in San Anton, isn't it?
: Is it? Well, I don't know.
Somewhere around there.
: Yeah.
Because they went from camp to camp. A lot of times they was stationed in other camps.
: Yeah. And --
And then they moved the tenth cavalry -- moved to Kansas.
: Yeah.
